title: A Song Is Born: everyone in Hollywood on the set
summary: Barnet recalls the 1948 film with Goodman, Armstrong, Tommy Dorsey and others, shot while each led a band nightly, stretching a two-week job to seven weeks.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: "Skyliner." Hey, it's a Snader Telescription, it's not Cowan. It's called, "Skyliner," 1951, three minutes. Snader telescription in which the title number was played by Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra. Claude Williams, -Sah piano, Bill Holman, tenor sax, Dave Wells, trombone, and Bob Dawes, baritone sax. And, "A Song is Born," 1948, Howard Hawks.
Oh, yeah. That's still on. You see that all the time.

I've seen that on television, yeah. Hawks's color remake of his own '41 movie, "Ball of Fire," itself an adaptation of Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs. Benny Goodman plays a leading role, supported by Louis Armstrong, Tommy Dorsey, Lionel Hampton, Charlie Barnet, Mel Powell, Harry Babasin, Benny Carter, Al Hendrickson, Louis Bellson, Buck Washington -- who's Buck Washington? And Kenny Dorne. -ham
Oh. Numbers include, "Flying Home," "Stealing Apples," and, "A Song is Born." Yeah, here's a --
Everybody in Hollywood was in that picture, all the musicians.

You know, that was quite a scene there. I was working at the Aragon Ballroom, and Tommy was working at the Casino Gardens, and Louis Lee Armstrong was working out at the Trianon, and Benny wasn't working anyplace, he got his sleep every night. But we'd crawl in and get a couple hours sleep, you know, and be at that studio, and it went on and on and on. Originally it was only supposed to be a two week gig. Well, we were on it seven weeks. So much so that my band finished the Aragon and MCA pulled some strings and let it open -- got the band to open up in Portland, at the Jansen Beach Ballroom without me, because it overlapped a few days. And that was where that famous fight was supposed to have taken place. I dont' know if you heard about it, between Tommy and Benny Goodman.
